data.body:
PHASE 2 COMPLETE — rebar-debug final report. Gerrit change 1963 (commit a13190d82c) is up for
review. No live Jira was touched at any point: every probe used `--collect-only`, so no test
body ran and no Jira request was issued.

## Test (RED -> GREEN, held out from the fixer)

`tests/unit/test_live_jira_xdist_confinement.py` — five tests, written and seen RED BEFORE any
fix existed, then physically moved out of the tree so the implementing subagent could not read
or edit it. It was handed only the proven mechanism and a contract card.

Legitimately RED first, for the right reason in both cases:
- the AST policy scan failed naming exactly one offender,
  `tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli.py::test_reconcile_dry_run_against_live_jira`, no false
  positives;
- the behavioural subprocess test failed with the unsafe configuration SILENTLY ACCEPTED —
  exit 0, "16 tests collected" — which is the defect itself, not an import or fixture error.
Three negative controls (loadgroup accepted, serial accepted, no-credentials silent) passed
before the fix and still pass after, so the guard's no-op cases are pinned too.

Teeth confirmed by three defect-seeded mutations, each re-introducing a confirmed cause and
each returning a DIFFERENT test to RED:
- re-remove the `xdist_group` decorator -> the policy scan goes RED;
- neuter the loadgroup check (`if dist == "loadgroup"` -> always-safe) -> the behavioural test
  goes RED;
- neuter the credentials check -> `test_guard_stays_silent_without_live_jira_credentials` goes
  RED, proving the CI-safety no-op is genuinely asserted and not incidental.

Refactoring litmus: the subprocess tests assert observable output (exit code + message text),
not internals — renaming `unconfined_live_jira_reason` does not break them.

## Fix

- `tests/interfaces/facades/test_cli.py` — `@pytest.mark.xdist_group("live_reconcile_e2e")` on
  `test_reconcile_dry_run_against_live_jira` (function decorator; module-scope `pytestmark`
  would be wrong, the file is overwhelmingly non-live).
- `tests/_live_jira_confinement.py` (new) — a PURE predicate
  `unconfined_live_jira_reason(config, items) -> str | None`. Returns a message only when the
  run is parallel AND the scheduler is not `loadgroup` AND live credentials plus `acli` are
  ACTUALLY present AND at least one collected item carries the group. Every other combination
  is a silent no-op. Kept out of conftest so it is callable without spawning pytest (and
  conftest is near this project's 800-line cap).
- `tests/conftest.py` — arm (c) on the existing `pytest_collection_modifyitems`, beside the
  bug-4a48 external-confinement guard it is modelled on. It raises `pytest.UsageError` rather
  than `pytest.fail`: this arm can only fire under `-n>0`, and from the xdist controller a
  `pytest.fail` escapes as a 20-line `INTERNALERROR>` traceback that buries the remedy under a
  stack the reader did not cause. I checked this empirically before changing it. The condition
  IS a usage error, so `UsageError` gives a clean `ERROR: …` banner at exit 4. A guard whose
  entire value is a legible message must not look like a crash.
- `tests/integration/test_reconcile_live_e2e.py` — comment-only. The old text closed "they also
  self-skip without live creds, so this only matters on a local live run", which promised
  protection exactly where it is absent. It now states the mark is honoured ONLY under
  `--dist loadgroup`, that other schedulers discard it silently, and that the guard covers the
  rest.

Explicitly NOT done: pinning `--dist loadgroup` in `pyproject.toml` addopts (AC1's suggested
option). Reasons in the RCA comment — addopts are prepended so CI's explicit `--dist worksteal`
still wins (fake protection in the very lane it appears to cover), it reschedules ~15k tests in
every local `-n` run, and it fixes neither gap.

## Replication of the original report

Run on THIS machine, which turns out to have live Jira credentials AND `acli` on PATH — i.e.
it is itself an instance of the exposed configuration, which is corroborating evidence for the
harm premise rather than a hypothetical.

- `pytest --collect-only -n auto` (the reporter's "complete local xdist inventory"; `auto`
  resolved to `-n 18` here, incidentally confirming docs/coverage.md's over-subscription
  warning) -> BEFORE: silently accepted. AFTER: exit 4 with the violation and the remedy.
- `pytest --collect-only -n 4` (bare, so xdist's default `--dist load`) -> exit 4.
- `pytest --collect-only -n 4 --dist loadgroup` -> exit 0, 15168 tests collected; the safe path
  is unobstructed.
- The group now holds **17** items where it held 16, which is the direct end-to-end proof that
  the previously-ungrouped live test joined it.

The original report no longer reproduces: the silent inertness is gone in every mode.

## Scope & safety

- Caller-dependency sweep: clear. Nothing references
  `test_reconcile_dry_run_against_live_jira` outside its own definition. The one caller that
  invokes a `pytest_collection_modifyitems` with `config=None`
  (`tests/unit/test_external_canary.py:92,100`) loads `tests/external/conftest.py`, NOT the root
  conftest, so it is untouched — I verified the import target rather than assuming from the
  symbol name.
- Restoration, not creation: no new entry point, user-visible artifact, or mutating external
  call. The guard is test infrastructure, and AC3 of this ticket is its design authority.
- No new dependency. No test weakened — the two edits to existing test files are one decorator
  plus comments; no assertion removed, none loosened, no skip/xfail added.

## Step 7 sweep

Axis 1 (construct). The new AST scan IS the repo-wide sweep for "a live-Jira-reaching test
without the group mark": it walks all of `tests/` except `tests/external/` and found exactly one
live instance, now fixed. One related-but-distinct construct found:
`xdist_group("large_ticket_server")` on two tests in
`tests/integration/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone.py:334,348` is inert under the same conditions.
Disposition: ACCEPTED, not fixed. It confines a LOCAL git-server fixture, so scattering costs
duplicate fixture setup, not correctness — a different severity class from racing a shared
external system.

Axis 2 (parity). Rule, stated without reference to the fixed site: "a test that can reach the
shared live Jira must be serialised against every other such test." Census over the surfaces
this rule can have — the test lanes, since this is a test-infra rule with no CLI/MCP/library
surface:
- default tier — `--dist worksteal`, but deselects `integration`, so no group item is ever
  collected. N/A.
- integration tier — `--dist loadgroup`. Covered by the added mark.
- external tier (`tests/external/`) — its own credential-scoped workflow job;
  `external-integration.yml` passes NO `-n` and NO `--dist`, so it is serial by construction.
  Verified, not assumed. N/A.
- e2e tier — no live Jira. N/A.
- dual-direction (a live-Jira test reaching Jira by some path other than `acli`) — probed every
  non-external test referencing `JIRA_URL`/`JIRA_API_TOKEN`; all are hermetic/mocked, and
  `tests/unit` + `tests/scripts` are socket-guarded by conftest's network guard. `acli` is the
  reconciler's only Jira transport. No MISSING slot.

## Residual risk

1. The detector keys on `which("acli")`. A future live-Jira test reaching Jira over direct HTTP
   would evade it. ACCEPTED: no such transport exists — `acli` is the reconciler's only Jira
   path, so adding one would be a deliberate architectural change that should carry its own
   confinement review.
2. `large_ticket_server`'s inert group, above. ACCEPTED, cost not correctness.
3. The guard cannot protect a machine with credentials that runs the live tests SERIALLY against
   a Jira project someone else is concurrently using. Out of scope: that is cross-process, not
   cross-worker.

## Gates

`make lint` PASS; `make typecheck` PASS (598 files); `check_complexity_baseline.py --check` ->
`active=49 new=0 increased=0 stale=0`. Pre-commit hook (lint + typecheck + 50/72 message wrap)
passed on commit. CI workflows untouched — the `--timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread` hang
guards and every existing `-n`/`--dist` argument are unchanged.

Local full default-suite run: started, and being left to run as corroboration, but it is slow on
this host (~15k tests) and CI's four-cell matrix is the authoritative broad regression oracle.
The ticket will NOT be closed before `Verified +1`.
